method: Read candidate fit JSON and packaged geometry; load same server registered runtime; call actual radius-aware support query. No original runtime, rendering, GPU or gameplay simulation executed.
reproduction: npx tsx -e 'import "./server/original-scenes"; import {getOriginalMapRuntime} from "./shared/originalMapRuntime"; const r=getOriginalMapRuntime("woodlands"),p={x:11.78469241646333,y:-4.174312729144826,z:39.01874104349856}; const support=r.geometry.playerSupportHeightAt(p.x,p.z,p.y,r.profile.radius,r.profile.bodyHeight); console.log({camera:p,support,eyeAboveSupport:support===undefined?null:p.y-support,sourceStandingEyeHeight:r.profile.eyeHeight});'
interpretation: The fitted eye is 5.12527 world units above recovered support rather than the source standing height of 1.72. This is inconsistent with a standing camera under the retained geometry; without evidence of an airborne original frame or a changed support surface, physical registration remains unproved.

versionEvidence.limits: The retrieval/archive date labels differ. They do not identify a changed game revision or prove any mesh difference. Asymmetric roof, open bay, broad/narrow doors and textures visibly agree at broad shape level. A geometry mismatch requires an independently identified older payload or repeatable feature discrepancy across frames.

limits: Manual pixel uncertainty understated semantic vertex identification risk; occluded eaves, jamb depth edges and soil/shadow transitions can be assigned to the wrong vertex.
The 15s fit residuals exceed most declared pixel uncertainties; those labels and fitted pose must remain failed candidates, not accepted by inflating uncertainties.

The solver fixes vertical focal length from full 574px frameheight, principalpoint at image center and FOV 50; unknown sprite rectangle/crop could invalidate that mapping even though source FOV 50 itself is supported.
The 16s frame gives larger clearer bay depth edges; independent fresh annotation may test identities without revising 15s heldout labels from fitted predictions.
